The [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]] is a seasonal [[association football]] competition established in 1962.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.concacaf.com/inside-concacaf/about-concacaf/history |title=History |publisher=Concacaf |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> From its foundation until 2008, it was known as the CONCACAF Champions' Cup. Prior to the [[2024 CONCACAF Champions Cup|2024 season]], the tournament was named the CONCACAF Champions League (2008–2023).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2023/06/06/concacaf-champions-cup-new-flagship-club-competition/ |title=Concacaf Champions Cup new flagship club competition |website=Jamaica Observer |date=6 June 2023 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> It is the top continental football competition organized by [[CONCACAF]] for clubs from North America, Central America and the Caribbean. The participating clubs qualify for the tournament, based on their performance in its national leagues. The competition has been held in 61 editions, from 1962 to 2026, with 63 titles awarded due to the shared title for three clubs in the [[1978 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1978 edition]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesc/cacups78.html |title=Copa de Campeones 1978 |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The tournament has had 30 clubs from nine nations, that have won at least one title, with Mexican clubs being the most successful with 14 clubs winning 41 titles in total.<ref name="RSSSF">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesc/ca1.html |title=CONCACAF Cup |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

From 1962 to 1991, the final was contested over [[Two-legged match|two legs]], one match at each stadium of the finalist clubs. [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]] won the inaugural edition in [[1962 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1962]], defeating [[Comunicaciones F.C.|Comunicaciones]] 6–0 on aggregate score.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.informador.mx/ideas/Chivas-y-el-titulo-de-Concacaf-una-historia-de-desencuentros-con-final-feliz-20180426-0014.html |title=Chivas y el título de Concacaf, una historia de desencuentros con final feliz |website=Informador |date=26 April 2018 |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es}}</ref> The first edition with a single final match played at a neutral venue was held in [[1992 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1992]], in which [[Club América|América]] defeated [[Liga Deportiva Alajuelense|Alajuelense]] at the [[Santa Ana Stadium]] in [[Santa Ana, California]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesc/cacups92.html#cc |title=Copa de Campeones 1992 |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> The format returned to two-legged matches from the [[2003 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2003 edition]], except for the [[2020 CONCACAF Champions League|2020 edition]] that was affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.orlandocitysc.com/news/orlando-s-exploria-stadium-host-final-stages-2020-scotiabank-concacaf-champions |title=Orlando’s Exploria Stadium to Host Final Stages of 2020 Scotiabank Concacaf Champions League |publisher=Orlando City SC |date=10 November 2020 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> In the [[2021 CONCACAF Champions League|2021]] and starting with the [[2024 CONCACAF Champions Cup|2024]] editions, a single-leg final match was played at the home of the club with the best performance in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.concacaf.com/news/concacaf-holds-36th-ordinary-congress |title=Concacaf holds 36th Ordinary Congress |publisher=Concacaf |date=23 October 2021 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

In 10 editions of the tournament, a final match for the title was not held (1963, 1968, 1970, 1973, 1978, 1980, 1984, 1993, 1995 and 1996).<ref name="RSSSF"/> In 16 editions, the final was contested between clubs from the same national association, with 15 finals between Mexican clubs ([[1996 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|1996]], [[2002 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2002]], [[2003 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2003]], [[2006 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2006]], [[2007 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2007]], [[2009 CONCACAF Champions League final|2009]], [[2010 CONCACAF Champions League final|2010]], [[2012 CONCACAF Champions League final|2012]], [[2013 CONCACAF Champions League final|2013]], [[2014 CONCACAF Champions League final|2014]], [[2016 CONCACAF Champions League final|2016]], [[2017 CONCACAF Champions League final|2017]], [[2019 CONCACAF Champions League final|2019]], [[2021 CONCACAF Champions League|2021]], and [[2026 CONCACAF Champions Cup|2026]]) and one final between Costa Rican clubs ([[2004 CONCACAF Champions' Cup|2004]]).<ref name="RSSSF"/>

[[Club América|América]] and [[Cruz Azul]] are the most successful in titles won, winning seven titles each, followed by [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] with six titles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesc/ca1.html#fin:~:text=Clubwise%20list%20of%20winners |title=CONCACAF Cup - Clubwise list of winners |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> Only four clubs have won two or more consecutive titles and all of them Mexican clubs, Cruz Azul is the only club to achieve it twice (1969, 1970, 1971 and 1996, 1997), Pachuca (2007, 2008), [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] (2011, 2012, 2013), and América (2015, 2016).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.futboltotal.com.mx/futbol-internacional/concachampions/que-equipos-mexicanos-han-ganado-la-concachampions-de-forma-consecutiva/2026/03/ |title=¿Qué equipos mexicanos han ganado la Concachampions de forma consecutiva? |publisher=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.concacaf.com/news/facts-and-figures-on-the-concacaf-champions-cup |title=Facts and figures on the Concacaf Champions Cup |publisher=Concacaf |date=12 January 2024 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

Pachuca were the last champions before the competition was renamed as CONCACAF Champions League in 2008, defeating [[Deportivo Saprissa|Saprissa]] 3–2 on aggregate score in the [[2008 CONCACAF Champions' Cup#Final|2008 finals]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tuzos.com.mx/campeon-concacaf-2008/ |title=Campeón Concacaf 2008 |publisher=Club de Fútbol Pachuca |access-date=27 July 2026 |language=es}}</ref> Under the Champions League format, only clubs from [[Liga MX]] and [[Major League Soccer]] (three clubs from the United States and two from Canada) have reached the final. From 2006 to 2021, all titles were won by Mexican clubs. [[Seattle Sounders FC]] became the first and only non-Mexican club to win the title under the name Champions League, defeating [[Pumas UNAM]] in the [[2022 CONCACAF Champions League final|2022 final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.soundersfc.com/news/immortality-sounders-become-first-mls-club-to-win-concacaf-champions-league |title=Immortality: Sounders become first MLS club to win Concacaf Champions League |publisher=Seattle Sounders FC |date=5 May 2022 |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>
